title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 54-56): Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' analysis situs through structures he calls 'ateliers' (workshops), (F, M, ◁, ≪°, |·|). Here F is a lattice of 'fragments' ordered by ≤, with Sup, Inf and ∩. M (also written 𝒰 on the next page) is a distinguished generating subset of 'elementary' fragments, ≪° is a relative-interior or 'strictly inside' relation, and |·| is a further incidence or boundary-type relation; p. 54 adds ∈. On p. 54 he decides to define homomorphisms of ateliers f : F → F'. This page lists the conditions.

(1) f should be monotone for ≤ and commute with arbitrary Sup. Every fragment is the Sup of the elementary fragments below it, so f is determined by its restriction f_M : M → F'. Explicitly, f(F) = Sup_{X∈M, X≤F} f_M(X), and f_M is monotone. Conversely, if the fragments of F are of finite type, or if F' is 'inconditionnel' (presumably admitting all the Sups needed), then every monotone f_M extends to such an f. This is the standard free-cocompletion / left-Kan-extension statement for a sup-lattice generated by a subposet.

(2) f should also commute with arbitrary Inf, including the empty Inf (so the top element is preserved; this is the correction 'familles d'indices vides'). To start, f should commute with binary meets: (*) f(F∩G) = f(F)∩f(G). By Sup-preservation this reduces to F, G elementary. The condition becomes (*)_M: f_M(X)∩f_M(Y) = Sup_{Z∈M, Z≤X∩Y} f_M(Z). He notes the analogy with the familiar formula for a set-theoretic cell decomposition ('fragmentation ensembliste'): X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k∈ij} X_k, the intersection of two closed cells being the union of the common cells.

(*) gives commutation with finite Inf. Infinite Inf then reduces to filtered decreasing families. The next page says it is not clear this must be imposed in the definition. Next he wants f_M compatible with ≪° and |·| even when f_M lands in F rather than in M, and proposes the condition (**): f induces an order isomorphism Ss(F) ≅ Ss(f(F)) on subfragments. He realises (**) would force f(M) ⊂ M'. He then hesitates, citing a counterexample (Example B, p. 50), which he judges heteroclite for dimension reasons.

The problem served: finding the right notion of morphism for his combinatorial/tame model of 'polyhedral' spaces in the 4th draft of Analysis situs.
errors: No mathematical error. The reduction of (*) to elementary F, G uses distributivity of ∩ over Sup in F', which must hold or be part of the axioms; this is implicit.
The extension claim in (1) needs Sup_{X≤F} f_M(X) to exist in F'. That is why the finite-type or 'inconditionnel' hypothesis is needed, and he states it.

Reducing infinite Inf to filtered decreasing families requires finite-meet preservation plus the commutation with filtered Inf. This is correct but left unverified ('pas clair que ce soit essentiel').

ideas.what: A Sup-preserving map out of a lattice generated by elementary fragments is determined by, and freely extended from, a monotone map on the generators.
ideas.modern_name: Left Kan extension / free sup-lattice (ideal completion) on a poset
ideas.where_published: Same pattern as extension of functors from a generating site in SGA 4 Exp. I-IV, not specifically for fragments

ideas.what: The meet-preservation condition expressed on generators: f(X)∩f(Y) = Sup_{Z≤X∩Y} f(Z).
ideas.modern_name: Flatness / covering-flatness condition. Equivalently, a map on a basis defining a frame homomorphism (morphism of locales).
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. IV (morphisms of topoi via flat functors); here specialised to lattices of fragments

ideas.what: Analogy with the intersection formula of cell decompositions, X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k∈ij} X_k.
ideas.modern_name: Regular cell complexes / face posets; stratification axiom
ideas.where_published: Tame-topology program sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism

ideas.what: Notion of 'atelier' and its homomorphisms (preserving ≤, Sup, Inf, ≪°, |·|, ∈), as a foundation for tame topology.
ideas.modern_name: Closest: o-minimal structures / semialgebraic cell decompositions; posets of strata; combinatorial models of tame spaces
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs manuscripts (cote 156)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's definition of morphisms of 'ateliers' (his combinatorial axiomatisation of tame spaces) is left open. He is undecided whether elementary fragments must go to elementary fragments, and whether commutation with infinite Inf is needed. The notion is not in the literature, but the local content of this page (Kan extension plus a flatness condition) is standard.
missed.quote: (*)_M f_M(X) ∩ f_M(Y) = Sup_{Z ∈ X∩Y} f_M(Z) (qui rappelle la formule familière pour une fragmentation ensembliste X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k∈ij} X_k)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a piece of the unrealised 1986 'tame topology' foundation. It could be compared with locale-theoretic or o-minimal approaches to defining maps of cell-decomposed spaces, but on its own it is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step in an unpublished axiomatisation. It extends monotone maps from generators by Sup and translates finite-meet preservation into a flatness-type condition on generators, which is well known from locale and topos theory. The only historical interest is that it documents Grothendieck's unpublished 'atelier' formalism for tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'par leur restriction aux f.o el.' is likely 'par leur restriction aux fragm. élém.' (elementary fragments).
'F, G sont des ... [?]' is probably 'F, G sont des élémentaires' (or similar), as the formula uses X, Y ∈ M.
In (*)_M the index set 'Z ∈ X∩Y' may carry tildes in the image; its meaning is Z elementary with Z ≤ X∩Y.
'familles d'indices vides' is correct: 'finies' is struck out and 'd'indices' inserted, so the meaning is that empty Inf (the top element) must be preserved.
The page number at the bottom is 64, the archive pagination.
